column4: Active since February 2022, across a roughly 750-mile front described by trackers as a stalemate outside a Ukrainian gain of about 100 square miles in Zaporizhzhia in February 2026 (the first month since 2023 in which Ukraine gained more territory than it lost). Two named truces in 2026 (April, May) each proved partial or collapsed; a May 2026 three-day ceasefire and prisoner exchange "quickly unraveled." On September 23 2026 senior officials of the Russian government "effectively rejected" a US-Ukrainian-proposed limited "energy" ceasefire (no strikes on power, heating or water infrastructure) and Russia's foreign minister stated operations would not pause during talks; a Russian helicopter's incursion into Polish airspace the same week read as a further escalation toward a NATO member. Both sides have floated resuming contact, possibly in October 2026, but no date or level of seniority is confirmed. Russia continues to demand Ukrainian withdrawal from part of Donbas plus recognition of occupied territory; Ukraine's government has offered only the narrower energy truce, now rejected.
column5: HIGH; already past four years with no resolution mechanism close to landing, and the one concrete proposal on the table this month (the limited energy truce) was rejected within days of being floated; a continuing war or an unstable truce is the safer 2029 baseline than a full peace settlement

column2: 2026 Iran war (US and Israel vs. Iran)
column4: Hostilities opened 2026-02-28 with joint US-Israeli strikes, after a currency-collapse protest crisis in Iran drew a US reinforcement pledge in January 2026. At least three named ceasefire attempts (April, June, and a further implied one) each collapsed within weeks to months; no ceasefire is in effect as of day 209 (September 24). On 2026-09-24 Iran's government formally submitted a written roadmap for a regionwide ceasefire of up to sixty days, a phased reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, an end to the blockade, the unfreezing of frozen assets and an agreed negotiating timeline, conveyed through Pakistani, Qatari and Egyptian mediation after direct US-Iran contact at the UN General Assembly (the first publicly acknowledged contact since June). Iran's Supreme National Security Council separately attached a four-to-five-day response deadline, which reads as inconsistent with the roadmap's own ceasefire-during-talks framing; domestic divisions were reported in Tehran over whether the talks were authorized. Iran's claim to have restored 60-70% of pre-war Strait of Hormuz flow is contradicted by independent shipping-transit data (one transit recorded September 20 against an approximately 85-a-day pre-war baseline; about 396 vessels idle in the watch zone under a "SEVERE" maritime advisory). No strikes, ballistic launches or drone attacks against the reading government's forces were reported for fifteen to nineteen consecutive days heading into September 24, an informal lull short of a declared ceasefire. Crude oil rose 3.9% to $103.08 on September 23 2026 — materially above the $91 August 2026 reading this program's price-anchors table carries from the EIA's September 9 outlook, a gap any D3/D11/D14 decision made after this date should account for rather than anchor on the stale figure.
column5: MODERATE-UNCERTAIN; the repeated-collapse pattern could resolve into a durable settlement well before 2029, or could persist as a low-boil blockade-and-strikes state; the September 24 roadmap is the most concrete proposal to date but carries its own internal contradiction (a short deadline bolted onto a longer framework) and disputed domestic authorization; either way the associated Iran sanctions program and an elevated Gulf force posture are likely still live at the oath even if active combat by then isn't

column4: A de jure ceasefire has been in effect since 2025-10-10 under Phase 1 of a US-backed peace plan, but it has been heavily violated on the ground per widely reported tallies. Phase 2 (armed-group disarmament) talks were stalled as of May 2026 over sequencing disputes.
column5: CONTESTED/THIN for a 2.4-years-out projection; the ceasefire LABEL is plausible to persist, continued low-level violation is very plausible, a genuine political resolution (disarmament, reconstruction, governance) is uncertain

column4: Opened 2026-03-02 with rocket fire into northern Israel, ground operations from 2026-03-16. A ceasefire took effect 2026-04-16 and was extended multiple times under US mediation. As of late July 2026 Israeli forces still held pockets of occupied southern Lebanese territory even as a phased, monitored withdrawal proceeded (the Lebanese army redeployed into one further town on 2026-07-21 after an Israeli pullback there). A June 26 2026 US-brokered framework requiring the armed group's full withdrawal and disarmament was rejected by that group on announcement; re-checked 2026-09-24 (second pass) and no fresher dated status than the July 21 milestone was found opened this session.
column5: MODERATE; an actively mediated, still-incomplete withdrawal-for-ceasefire process; plausibly settled into a stable line by 2029, but the underlying file is decades old and has reignited before

column2: Sudan civil war (Sudanese Armed Forces vs. Rapid Support Forces)
column4: Listed as a top-tier 2026 watch item: "civil war escalation with mass atrocities and regional spillover." Fighting has run since April 2023. Widely reported (not independently verified this session) casualty and displacement figures describe one of the world's largest current displacement crises.
column5: HIGH; matches the long-duration, no-functioning-resolution-mechanism profile of the sub-Saharan Africa civil-war bucket in war-durations.tsv (median about 9 years); a multi-year continuation past 2029 is the safer default

column2: Myanmar civil war (military government vs. resistance and ethnic armed organizations)
column4: Listed as a top-tier 2026 watch item: "military junta clashes accelerating state collapse," compounded by intensified criminal economy activity. Fighting has run since the February 2021 takeover.
column5: HIGH; matches the Asia-region civil-war bucket in war-durations.tsv, the single longest-duration region in that sample (median about 12 years)

column2: DRC conflict (M23/AFC-led alliance vs. government, with reported Rwanda backing)
column4: Fighting reignited in 2021; the alliance captured the provincial capitals of two major eastern cities in early 2025. A framework agreement was signed in Doha in November 2025. A follow-on peace roadmap (sequenced steps, standardized ceasefire-violation reporting, an implementation-dispute mechanism) was agreed 2026-08-21 after Switzerland-mediated talks involving the DRC, the alliance, the US, Qatar, Togo, Switzerland and the African Union. A ceasefire-verification mission was due in one contested district the following week. Fighting, including a reported drone strike causing civilian casualties, continued on the very day the roadmap was announced.
column5: MODERATE-HIGH; an active, US-brokered diplomatic track exists, but implementation is already visibly leaking; continued low-intensity conflict or an uneasy monitored peace is more likely than a clean resolution by 2029

column2: Sahel jihadist insurgency (Mali, with regional spillover to Burkina Faso and Niger)
column4: Listed as a 2026 watch item: "growing insurgencies across the Sahel (especially in Mali)." Supplementary reporting (not independently opened this session) describes militant pressure on Mali's capital, fuel-supply disruption and social restrictions imposed by militants in early September 2026.
column5: HIGH; chronic, worsening, multi-country insurgency with no functioning resolution mechanism visible in the record

column4: On 2026-01-03 a US military operation captured Venezuela's then-president and his spouse; both were taken to the United States and indicted on narco-trafficking and related charges. Venezuela's vice president was sworn in as acting president on 2026-01-05, the first woman to hold the role. Reported deaths in the operation numbered roughly 80 across Venezuelan security personnel, foreign (Cuban) military/intelligence personnel present in-country, and a small number of wounded US personnel. Oil-sector sanctions were substantially eased through general licenses, and the IMF resumed engagement with Venezuela in April 2026 after most voting members recognized the acting administration. On 2026-09-24 the acting president told the UN General Assembly that elections would eventually be held but gave no date, and separately met the US president to discuss debt restructuring and diplomatic normalization; the same week, at the UN, Venezuela's government called for direct negotiation with Guyana over the Essequibo dispute rather than deferring to the pending ICJ ruling (see dyads.tsv VEN-GUY, source S55).
column5: UNCERTAIN, BUT LIKELY RESOLVED ONE WAY OR ANOTHER BY 2029; three years is enough time for either a stabilized, election-legitimized government or a relapse into instability if elections keep slipping; the sanctions-relief and normalization trend already underway looks more durable than the acute crisis itself

column4: PLA aircraft-incursion tempo eased substantially from a 2024-25 peak by mid-2026, alongside direct US-China leader-level engagement earlier in the year. A revised PRC National Defense Mobilization Law takes effect 2026-10-01, reportedly broadening the cases in which China could invoke wartime civilian-asset mobilization below the threshold of open war. The China Coast Guard maintains a more assertive standing presence in waters east of Taiwan than before.
column5: HIGH that elevated-but-below-war tension persists in some form (this is a multi-decade structural condition); the specific intensity three years out is not safely projectable turn to turn

column4: Multiple ballistic-missile and other weapons tests were reported in April 2026, and a hypersonic-missile test was reported in September 2026 (not independently opened this session).
